name: concordance_company_brief
description:
The cross-source correlation endpoint: joins market quotes (3
providers), SEC filings, and general mentions (news/academic/legal/
dev-community) for one company in a single call -- something no
single-source competitor in this space can offer, since it requires
owning all the underlying sources already. Partial results are
normal and expected here (e.g. market data present but no recent
filings) -- this endpoint aggregates across inherently-optional
sources, unlike /tools/series which is about exactly one source and
where "not synced yet" is a meaningful 503 signal. Cost: ~$0.05/call [spec].

company.title: Company
company.description: Ticker (AAPL) or company name (Apple). Coverage is a bounded vendor watchlist.

name: concordance_corroboration
description:
Is this claim independently corroborated across multiple unrelated
sources, or does it trace back to a single origin? Groups matches by
SOURCE (not category, unlike /tools/digest) so a caller can see exactly
how many independent outlets/agencies/publications back a claim, not
just how many raw documents mention it -- the literal meaning of
"concordance": where a claim is attested across a body of independently
sourced texts. Cost: ~$0.04/call [spec].

name: concordance_digest
description:
The cross-category synthesis endpoint: one call replaces manually
calling /tools/search once per category and merging results
yourself. Deliberately NOT an LLM-generated summary -- pure
structured aggregation of real search hits, keeping the same zero-
marginal-cost model as the rest of this service (an LLM call here
would need its own paid API key and per-call cost, undermining the
whole "free sources, free to run" design). Cost: ~$0.03/call [spec].

name: concordance_help
description: Extended documentation for all concordance_* tools: API-wide usage guidance, pricing notes, and workflows published by the vendor (llms.txt). Takes no arguments and returns the full document. Call this before other concordance_* tools when unsure how to use them.

name: concordance_search
description: Full-text search across every aggregated data source in one call: news, SEC filings, court opinions, academic papers, government records, and developer discussions. One query surfaces everything concordant across independently-sourced, citable results (source, category, title, content, url, published_at) -- not a single-source wrapper. Optional source/category/since filters; limit 1-100 (default 20). $0.01 per call.

name: concordance_series
description: Tabular time-series lookup by source + series_id: economic indicators (FRED, World Bank, UN Comtrade), crypto TVL (DefiLlama), weather (open_meteo), and stock quotes (finnhub/twelvedata/polygon). Optional start/end date range; returns [{observed_at, value}] points. $0.01 per call. Source slugs and series ids are listed in the param notes; the vendor's free /catalog endpoint has the live list.

series_id.title: Series Id
series_id.description: Vendor series id, e.g. fred: GDP, CPIAUCSL, UNRATE, FEDFUNDS, DGS10; world_bank: US-NY.GDP.MKTP.CD (<COUNTRY>-<indicator>). The vendor's free /catalog endpoint lists every live series.

source.title: Source
source.description: Catalog source slug: arxiv, core, courtlistener, defillama, finnhub, gdelt, govinfo, hackernews, open_meteo, polygon, regulations_gov, sec_edgar, stackexchange, twelvedata, un_comtrade, wikipedia, world_bank, fred.

name: concordance_timeline
description:
How has coverage of this topic developed over time, across every
aggregated source? Chronologically ordered (oldest first), unlike
/tools/search (relevance-ranked) or /tools/digest (grouped by
category) -- for tracking a story's evolution or an emerging trend
across independently-sourced outlets. Cost: ~$0.03/call [spec].
